answer: In each epoch, an agent deposits bonded stake and joins a Semaphore-style zero-knowledge identity tree, then evaluates the epoch polynomial to derive a rate-limited nullifier and commitment for each message. Reusing a nullifier creates two polynomial points with the same secret, allowing Shamir interpolation to recover the signing private key; the protocol treats this duplicate signal as proof of equivocation and instantly slashes collateral, making sybil identities costly to forge at every vertex.
